title: Maximal Intersection
description: You are given n segments on the number line. Your task is to remove exactly one segment such that the intersection of the remaining (n−1) segments has the maximal possible length. Determine this maximal length.
input_format: The first line contains a single integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 3 × 10^5) — the number of segments. Each of the next n lines contains two integers l_i and r_i (0 ≤ l_i ≤ r_i ≤ 10^9) — the left and right endpoints of the i-th segment.
output_format: Output a single integer — the maximal possible length of the intersection of the remaining (n−1) segments after removing exactly one segment.
expected_approach: To solve this problem, we need to find the maximal intersection of (n−1) segments after removing one segment. We can achieve this by maintaining prefix and suffix arrays that store the maximum left endpoint and minimum right endpoint of the segments up to a certain index. By removing a segment, we can calculate the intersection of the remaining segments using these arrays and determine the maximal length.

test_cases.explanation: By removing the segment [3;3], the intersection of the remaining segments is [2;3], which has a length of 1.
By removing either the segment [1;3] or [2;6], the intersection of the remaining segments is [2;4], which has a length of 2.
No matter which segment is removed, the intersection of the remaining segments is empty, resulting in a length of 0.
By removing the segment [1;5], the intersection of the remaining segments is [3;10], which has a length of 7.
